reviews.author: JózefM
reviews.title: Cool app! Trying to figure out how to use the shopping features
reviews.content: Really enjoy using this app! I appreciate how supportive and kind the developers are towards English-speaking users despite them not being the main user market. Unfortunately, my knowledge of Chinese is *extremely* limited so having built-in translation for the UI is so very helpful! Thanks for accommodating us and welcoming users outside China to the app. I realize this is a stretch and only offer it as a suggestion, but it would be really fantastic if the shopping functions of the app were made more user-friendly for English speakers in the future. I couldn’t figure it out since some of the interface didn’t auto translate and got overwhelmed. I’m not sure if things can be shipped to me in the USA among other details. Additionally, and I totally understand this is unlikely and once again only respectfully suggest it, I would love if I could pay with PayPal since I’ve seen some wonderful art I want to purchase but I buy everything online via PayPal and I don’t have any other payment app accounts to pay with. Completely understand that PayPal isn’t as common in China though and that it would be a feature primarily for international users. Just wanted to put it out there as a suggestion but understand if it cannot be implemented! Very nice app with a friendly community 👍 Will continue to use it

reviews.author: cyk110
reviews.title: The moment Americans see the real world
reviews.content: The sudden popularity of this app (RedNote) in the U.S. has sparked an unexpected cultural exchange between Chinese and American users. Many Americans see this as a rare chance to step outside the carefully curated bubble of U.S. capitals and media-controlled platforms and experience a more unfiltered, diverse world. For some, this is the first time they feel like they’re seeing a global perspective untouched by the influence of American algorithms or corporate agendas. Traditionally, the U.S. is portrayed as a beacon of diversity, but critics argue that American social media platforms often promote a sanitized, homogeneous version of the world. Algorithms are designed to maximize engagement, often feeding users what they want to see—or what corporations and governments want them to see—rather than offering a truly diverse flow of information. This has led to an increasingly narrow perception of the world for many Americans. In contrast, RedNote's content feels fresh and authentic, offering glimpses into real lives and cultures outside of the typical Western narrative. For many users, this is a wake-up call, exposing them to perspectives and stories they’ve never encountered. It’s ironic that, in seeking freedom from perceived U.S. media manipulation, many have turned to a Chinese platform to rediscover what diversity and authenticity truly mean.

They learned English so they could speak with us, the APP developers even made translation available for us. Thanks to the videos and people I stopped feeling anxiety, first they helped me calm down with funny videos. Then they showed me news, showing me that people around the world knew what was going on they wanted to help us. I felt a sense of relief seeing that it wasn’t as hopeless and TikTok MAGA was showing, there are still good people around. I deleted my TikTok and never looked back. I don’t post videos on here yet as I’m still learning but I’m not going to leave. There are so many wonderful people and friends I’ve been making and hope to keep making.

reviews.author: NOLA_Rainbeaux
reviews.title: I love it, but need to figure out how to translate
reviews.content: The Chinese people are so kind and friendly, so willing to share their culture with us, that the whole TikTok debacle ended up being a blessing! The exchange of ideas, history and culture between Americans and Chinese on Red Note is, I believe, an important and historical event. Some of the “Welcome, TikTok Refugees” posts brought me to tears. My only complaint is that I cannot find a way to translate within the app. I can’t read the buttons, so I don’t know what to click! I have had to copy and paste everything to Google Translate. I was able to translate the rules and regulations, because there was a “translate” button that popped up when I highlighted sections of the content. But on the “Creator Center”, I could not highlight anything to get that translator button up. I am hoping the creators will see the need for easier translation capabilities once they realize thousands of Americans have gone to their app from TikTok. Being able to communicate with the Chinese people is so exciting to me that even if TikTok returns, I will keep my Red Note account for as long as the Chinese let me! I highly recommend!

reviews.author: The dancing lobsters

reviews.content: For years as an American, I have been riddled with ads on ads on ads, thinking that this was the normal for society, thinking this was the normal worldwide when apparently it is not the normal. reviews.author: Its_Izzy 艾莎
reviews.title: Truly magical
reviews.content: I have never truly loved and enjoyed a social media platform more than Xiaohongshu. What I found here was much more than videos and posts. I discovered the kindness of the Chinese people, endless knowledge, rich history, beautiful traditions, and genuine hearts. There is something truly magical about this platform. As someone watching from far away, I am constantly amazed and inspired by the people, culture, and stories shared every day. The more time I spend on Xiaohongshu, the more connected I feel to the people here. What started as simply using an app became something much deeper. I met new friends who have become like family to me, and their warmth and friendship have touched my heart in ways I never expected. In fact, I left all other social media platforms and chose to keep only Xiaohongshu. For me, it is not just an app—it has become a special place filled with memories, friendships, learning, and inspiration. It will forever hold a place in my heart. Every day I learn something new about China—its history, culture, food, landscapes, and people. My admiration for this beautiful country grows more and more. I sincerely hope and pray that one day I can visit China, meet my dear friends in person, and experience the breathtaking scenery and rich culture with my own eyes. Thank you to everyone who has shared their lives, knowledge, and kindness here. You may not realize it, but you have made someone on the other side of the world feel welcomed, connected, and inspired. With love from afar. ❤️

reviews.author: sdGwan
reviews.title: Censorship Disguised as Moderation
reviews.content: I tried to post a heartfelt message on Xiaohongshu, but it kept getting deleted for no reason. This is what I wrote: When he was a child, his mother woke up early to push a cart selling naan to support him. He would secretly watch her back from inside the cart and silently promise himself to give her a better life. Later, after working hard as an actor, he bought her an apartment with a balcony where she could grow flowers. Every year the roses bloom, and the wind still passes gently through the balcony, but the one who promised to stay with his mother until old age will never come back. His mother will never again wait for him in this world. We don’t believe it, we all know it, but we are powerless. That is the tragedy of being small and voiceless. Please, can someone care? It’s a real human life. He was just the son of an ordinary family, and his mother is still waiting for him to come home. From Beijing to Xinjiang is so far—can he still find his way back? And during the time he was sidelined, he even donated 500,000 yuan to disaster relief under his own name, and went to volunteer teaching. He was truly a good person. Please help him! Don’t let the attention fade!

reviews.author: hsjebel
reviews.title: Social media that doesn’t rot your brain (unless you are into that)
reviews.content: A lovely and intuitive app, Its like what social media was meant to be before it all became a nightmare of adds and toxicity. The community is wonderful. Very friendly! There is a great sense of humor with good natured teasing, useful insight, and a genuine willingness to connect and learn. There are creators and netizens from around the world coming together sharing their art, culture, passions, and generally giving glimpses into what their life is like. It’s not the place to be a troll or needlessly stir up bad faith drama. The report button actually works, with feedback/follow-up letting you know how the issues resolved. The algorithm is very responsive to your actual interests, and you have the option to review the topics it is feeding you. The current translation feature(from the English speaking side) is currently only English-Chinese, and seems to work very well with only a few mishaps here and there which is to be expected. I do hope they expand this to more languages in the future, but for now, I’m enjoying the opportunity to work on my Spanish They recently opened the store to foreigners. In theory, this would be a great opportunity to have more direct access to goods that don’t have a middle man cutting quality for profits, and get honest reviews from everyday people, but with the economy being on fire… Anyways it’s a great app, if you are tired of being fed inflammatory slop, on platforms filled with trolls, give this a try!

reviews.author: Chase from Alabama
reviews.title: One of the Best
reviews.content: I joined this app in January 2025 when a lot of Americans joined. Unlike a lot of Americans, I never left. RedNote is a lot calmer, there isn’t near as much drama as some of the other apps, and more importantly, I’m finding a community of like minded people - I enjoy jade, beading, and tea, all of which I have found on RedNote. In fact, within a week or two of joining RedNote, I signed up for Mandarin lessons. And now, I’m planning a trip to China in 2026 to tour jade markets and tea gardens. Also, I don’t want to get too political, but my eyes have truly been opened to all of the anti-China propaganda that the West likes to pander to westerners. In truth, China is a lot more like the West than Europe and the U.S. would want us to believe. They have all levels of education, economics, ideologies. China is not the boogeyman that the West would like them to be. In closing, I love this app. I enjoy getting to see a different part of the world and make new international friends. Five out of Five Stars.

reviews.author: Hui Qian Zhang

reviews.author: Zuckerberg scam
reviews.title: Amazing connection and friendliness
reviews.content: I never knew that a social app could be this authentically friendly and interested in creating/maintaining a real user-oriented community. Red Note is a cross between TikTok and Instagram but better. Red Note is more interested in providing optimal experience for the user — as an example, when Red Note found out that thousands of Americans were flocking to their platform, they developed seamless translation functions. I’m learning so much about other cultures and experiences, and learning that we’re all human and all have the same basic needs - it is also prompting a self-discovering of some complicated feelings about the U.S. and a reexamination of our country values. Bottom line is that this app doesn’t have any bullying or intentional misinformation. It’s also not filled with advertisements. Join Red Note and continue learning, laughing, creating and connecting with others like you were on TikTok :)

reviews.author: Kaweraklu
reviews.title: A Beautiful App for Connection, Learning, and Cultural Exchange
reviews.content: I absolutely love Xiaohongshu / Little Red Book! The posts from Chinese users are not only funny and silly but also filled with warmth and kindness. The community is so welcoming and inclusive, creating an environment that feels like home. I joined the app before the TikTok ban, and while some hoped we’d all return to Facebook and Instagram, when the ban came into affect, that’s not the case for me. Xiaohongshu / Little Red Book has been a turning point in my life. It’s amazing to see China’s breathtaking beauty—from the bright lights of the cities to the serene countryside. As someone who lives paycheck to paycheck, it’s incredible to experience a place I’ll likely never visit and connect with the people there. The app has also been a window into both the United States and China, showing the lives of ordinary people in both places. I feel like we’re witnessing history in the making. Despite the hatred that exists in the world, Xiaohongshu / Little Red Book shows that we are all humans who want peace, love and acceptance with curiosity of others in the world around us. Even if TikTok returns, I’ll continue to use Xiaohongshu. It’s been a source of joy, learning, and connection. From discovering new recipes to understanding Chinese culture, I’ve learned so much and made new friends along the way. I truly hope our government doesn’t take this app away from us. It’s an amazing platform, and I highly recommend it to anyone who wants to broaden their horizons and experience something truly special.

reviews.author: encajeperro
reviews.title: Red Note: The Next Big Thing in Social Media
reviews.content: With TikTok no longer around, Red Note has quickly become the go-to app, and for good reason. It’s more than just a replacement—Red Note brings a fresh, creative energy to social media that’s absolutely addictive. The app is beautifully designed, blending vibrant aesthetics with a seamless user experience. From sharing videos to participating in trending challenges, it offers a dynamic platform that’s fun, engaging, and highly interactive. The unique features, like customizable templates, AI-powered editing tools, and live interactions, elevate content creation to a whole new level. What really sets Red Note apart is the community. The app has brought together an incredibly warm, creative, and supportive space where people can express themselves. The Chinese creators and users on the app have been amazing, sharing not only stunning content but also cultural insights that are enriching and inspiring. Their positivity and creativity are helping shape Red Note into a platform that celebrates diversity while connecting people from all over the world. The team behind Red Note clearly knows what they’re doing, and it’s exciting to see how fast it’s evolving. reviews.author: WanderingIsles
reviews.title: AI-Generated Content, Privacy Concerns, and Social Limitations
reviews.content: Xiaohongshu (RED) combines content sharing and social networking, but in practice it has several issues that make it unsuitable for genuine social interaction or friendships. Many posts are AI-generated, reducing content authenticity and making it hard for users to verify information, while popular posts may be supported by bots, increasing the risk of being misled. New accounts are often restricted almost immediately after registration, limiting posting, following, or commenting, and lifting these restrictions typically requires submitting real ID documents, raising serious privacy concerns. Social interactions are also superficial, as private messaging and comments are dominated by AI-driven or bot interactions, making it difficult to form meaningful connections. Overall, while Xiaohongshu may be appealing for lifestyle browsing and content consumption, widespread AI-generated content, immediate account restrictions, mandatory real ID verification, and shallow social interactions make it unsuitable for authentic communication and real social connections.

I will say, though, that reporting behavior is a bit challenging, since much of those pages are still in mandarin without English options, as far as I know. As of April 2025. All of this being said, I give Rednote a full 5 stars due to the receptiveness to feedback from their members and their quick action in making the app more user friendly for non mandarin speaking audiences.

reviews.author: Daquan Williams
reviews.title: Poor English Translation
reviews.content: I wanted to give Xiao Hon Shu a fair chance as it seemed like an interesting platform, but unfortunately, the overall experience was disappointing. First, the English translation quality is extremely poor throughout the app. Many menus, buttons, and system messages are either awkwardly translated or left entirely in Chinese, making navigation difficult for non-Chinese speakers. reviews.author: zzzzzzozzzzzz
reviews.title: Use Rednote, and experience the most laughable censorship imaginable.
reviews.content: As a 10-year user of Rednote, watching it sink deeper into its power of censorship honestly makes me sick. Anything posted on Rednote will go through their internal “review” before it can be publicly seen. If they don’t like your content but can’t justify banning it, they just make it invisible. You can see it on your own profile but no one else can. They do the same thing with comments too. If you ever feel like you left a thoughtful remark but get zero likes or replies, it was Rednote shadow-banning it. What’s worse is the complete lack of any consistent standard. One day they approve something, the next day you get a warning saying it “violates Rednote rules.” You can repost the exact same thing and, hilariously, most of the time it gets approved again. Then, days or even weeks later, Rednote randomly decides to take it down and hit you with another warning. This loop can repeat endlessly. No explanation, no transparency, no accountability. It is so ridiculous that almost feels like the moderation team has KPIs to hit, so they decided to go back and keep re-banning the contents themselves approved in the first place. Even the law has “non bis in idem”—no double punishment—but Rednote goes beyond that. Rednote has poured massive effort into marketing itself globally, but at its core the team just runs the app like a dictator. Making up rules on the spot and enforcing censorship so absurd that feels like a joke.
